title: Billy Diamond
wikitext:
{{Short description|Cree chief (1949–2010)}}
'''Billy Diamond''' (May 19, 1949 – September 30, 2010<ref>{{cite web|title=Respected Leader and former Grand Chief of the Crees of Quebec, Chief Dr. Billy Diamond, passes away this morning, on Thursday, September 30, 2010, in his home community of Waskaganish, Quebec |author=Grand Council of the Crees |date=30 September 2010 |access-date=2010-09-30 |url=http://www.newswire.ca/en/releases/archive/September2010/30/c6986.html}}</ref>) was the Chief of the [[Waskaganish, Quebec]] Cree from 1970 to 1976,<ref name=ce>{{cite encyclopedia|url=https://www.thecanadianencyclopedia.ca/en/article/billy-diamond|title=Billy Diamond |encyclopedia=[[The Canadian Encyclopedia]]|access-date=August 31, 2019}}</ref> the Grand Chief of the [[Grand Council of the Crees]] from 1974 to 1984, and a successful businessman who founded [[Air Creebec]].<ref>{{cite book |last=MacGregor|first=Roy|title=Chief: The Fearless vision of Billy Diamond |year=1989|publisher=[[Viking Press]] | url=https://archive.org/details/chieffearlessvis0000macg |url-access=registration|isbn=0-670-82735-5}}</ref><ref name="naaf">{{cite web |url=http://www.naaf.ca/html/b_diamond_e.html |title=Chief Billy Diamond, Business and Commerce |access-date=2008-02-03 |publisher=[[Indspire|National Aboriginal Achievement Foundation]] |archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20071103005551/http://www.naaf.ca/html/b_diamond_e.html <!-- Bot retrieved archive --> |archive-date = 2007-11-03}}</ref>

Diamond was elected Chief of the [[Waskaganish, Quebec|Cree Nation of Waskaganish]] at the age of 21.<ref name=ptc>{{cite web |url=http://www.powertochange.ie/changed/bdiamond.html |title=Billy Diamond |access-date=2008-02-03 |publisher=Power To Change |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080127111027/http://www.powertochange.ie/changed/bdiamond.html |archive-date=2008-01-27 }}</ref><ref name=ce/> On November 11, 1975, he signed [[The James Bay and Northern Quebec Agreement]] with the Canadian government.<ref>{{cite news |title=Interview with Billy Diamond and Roy MacGregor |url=https://www.umanitoba.ca/cm/cmarchive/vol17no4/interviewwithbillydiamond.html |publisher=CM Archive |access-date=2008-02-03 }}</ref> Using funds from the settlement, he created [[Air Creebec]], Cree Construction Company Limited, and Cree Yamaha Motors.<ref name=naaf/> For his outstanding achievements, Billy Diamond was appointed as a Chevalier into the [[Ordre National du Quebec]] in 1987.<ref name="ordre-national.gouv.qc.ca">{{Cite web|url=https://www.ordre-national.gouv.qc.ca/membres/membre.asp?id=211|title=Billy Diamond – Ordre national du Québec|website=www.ordre-national.gouv.qc.ca|access-date=2019-06-22}}</ref> On March 19, 1990, Diamond was a guest on ''100 Huntley Street''.<ref name="100huntley">{{Citation|last=100huntley|title=Flashback: Billy Diamond|date=2015-09-08|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=GmVzr-LRCL4 |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/varchive/youtube/20211221/GmVzr-LRCL4 |archive-date=2021-12-21 |url-status=live|access-date=2019-06-22}}{{cbignore}}</ref>

Diamond died at the age of 61 from a heart attack. In accordance with his instructions, his tombstone reads: "Gone to a meeting - will return."<ref name=GM>{{Cite news|url=https://www.theglobeandmail.com/news/national/billy-diamond-saviour-of-the-dammed/article1214694|title=Billy Diamond, saviour of the dammed|access-date=August 31, 2019}}</ref>

== Early life ==
Billy Diamond was born to Hilda and Malcolm Diamond<ref name=was>{{Cite web|url=https://waskaganish.ca/billy-diamond|title=Billy Diamond in his own words|website=Cree Nation of Waskaganish|access-date=August 31, 2019}}</ref> on May 17, 1949, in a tent near [[Rupert House]], Quebec, on the shore of [[James Bay]].<ref>{{cite book|url=https://archive.org/details/chronologyofnati00duan|url-access=registration|title=Chronology of Native North American History|last=Champagne|first=Duane|publisher=[[Gale Research]]|year=1994|isbn=0-8103-9195-3}}</ref> He grew up in the Cree Nation of Waskaganish (then Rupert House) until being forced to attend<ref name=was/> Bishop Horden Hall, a [[Canadian Indian residential school system|residential school]] in [[Moose Factory]], [[Ontario]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.trc.ca/about-us/residential-school.html|title=Truth and Reconciliation Commission of Canada (TRC) - Our Mandate|website=www.trc.ca|access-date=2019-06-22}}</ref> Diamond recalled that his hair was cut for the first time in his life immediately upon arrival, and the clothes his mother gave him were confiscated.<ref name=was/> Additionally, the students were punished if they attempted to communicate to each other in Cree.<ref name=was/> Despite these circumstances, Diamond achieved leadership awards while becoming interested in a variety of academic topics.<ref name=was/> As a teenager, he attended high school in [[Sault Ste. Marie, Ontario|Sault Ste. Marie]], Ontario, where he organized an Indian Students Council.<ref name="Billy Diamond footprints">{{Cite web|url=https://ammsa.com/publications/windspeaker/billy-diamond-footprints|title=Billy Diamond [footprints]|website=Ammsa.com|language=en|access-date=2019-06-22}}</ref><ref name=was />

== Political career ==
Diamond returned to Waskaganish after high school, serving as the Band Manager during the 1960s.<ref name=ce/> Although he personally hoped to attend law school, Diamond followed his father's wishes and successfully ran for Chief.<ref name=GM/> He was elected in 1970 at 21 years old, the youngest Chief in Canada at that time.<ref name=GM/> He helped to establish the [[Grand Council of the Crees]] in 1974, of which he was elected Grand Chief at age 23.<ref name="Timeline">{{Cite web|url=https://www.cngov.ca/community-culture/timeline/|title=Timeline|website=The Grand Council of the Crees (Eeyou Istchee)|language=en-US|access-date=2019-06-22}}</ref> As such, he represented Quebec Crees in the [[Assembly of First Nations]].<ref name="ordre-national.gouv.qc.ca"/> Diamond also helped to negotiate Sections 25 and 35 of the [[Canadian Charter of Rights and Freedoms]] from 1980 to 1983.<ref name=was/>

== Legacy ==

=== The James Bay and Northern Quebec Agreement ===
In 1971, [[Robert Bourassa|Premier Robert Bourassa]] announced that $6 billion hydroelectric dam would be built on the [[Eastmain River]] in Cree and Inuit territory, which he coined the "project of the century".<ref name="Timeline"/> The project was planned without consulting Cree and Inuit stakeholders, and would have flooded traditional Cree and Inuit hunting grounds.<ref name="JBNQA">{{Cite web|url=https://www.makivik.org/corporate/history/jbnqa/|title=JBNQA|website=Makivik Corporation|language=en-US|access-date=2019-06-22}}</ref> Diamond organized a meeting of James Bay Crees to discuss the urgency of this project, wherein they decided to challenge the government legally.<ref name=GM/> Initially, the court ruling in favour of the Inuit and Cree case was overturned.<ref name="JBNQA"/> However, Diamond and other Indigenous activists such as the [[Northern Quebec Inuit Association]] were able to secure an out-of-court settlement with [[Hydro-Québec|Hydro Quebec]] now known as the [[James Bay and Northern Quebec Agreement]] (JBNQA) in 1975.<ref name="JBNQA"/> This agreement allowed an altered hydroelectric project to be built in exchange for solidified land rights and financial compensation.<ref name="Timeline"/> The JBNQA is considered the first "Modern Treaty" and provided the James Bay Cree and Inuit with $225 million in compensation, in addition to investment infrastructure.<ref name="Timeline"/><ref name="Billy Diamond footprints"/>

=== Air Creebec ===
Diamond established [[Air Creebec]] in 1982, and served as its president.<ref name="ordre-national.gouv.qc.ca"/> The airline fulfills Diamond's vision of allowing the people of James Bay greater mobility, connecting coastal communities to larger urban centres such as Timmins, Val D'or, and Montreal.<ref name="aircreebec.ca">{{Cite web|url=https://www.aircreebec.ca/2017/07/01/bonjour-tout-le-monde/|title=Taking wing Starting an airline from scratch takes courage and determination|date=2017-07-01|website=Air Creebec|language=en-US|access-date=2019-06-22}}</ref> To this day, it is entirely Cree-owned.<ref name="aircreebec.ca"/>

== Personal life ==
Billy Diamond and his wife Elizabeth had six children.<ref name="Billy Diamond footprints"/> Later in life, he became a devout Christian.<ref name="100huntley"/><ref name="Billy Diamond footprints"/>

Billy Diamond (May 19, 1949 – September 30, 2010) was the Chief of the Waskaganish, Quebec Cree from 1970 to 1976, the Grand Chief of the Grand Council of the Crees from 1974 to 1984, and a successful businessman who founded Air Creebec.
Diamond was elected Chief of the Cree Nation of Waskaganish at the age of 21. On November 11, 1975, he signed The James Bay and Northern Quebec Agreement with the Canadian government. Using funds from the settlement, he created Air Creebec, Cree Construction Company Limited, and Cree Yamaha Motors. For his outstanding achievements, Billy Diamond was appointed as a Chevalier into the Ordre National du Quebec in 1987. On March 19, 1990, Diamond was a guest on 100 Huntley Street.
Diamond died at the age of 61 from a heart attack. In accordance with his instructions, his tombstone reads: "Gone to a meeting - will return."
